decisions.evidence: R2 maker summarizes rediscovery only as “search, your own tags”; R2 client adds that the list must show “title… description… tags… site icon, all right there.”
decisions.note: At goal alignment, the client supplied the missing readability-first list requirement.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker's goal summary does not specify opening saved links; R2 client adds that “clicking one just takes me to the actual page.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing original-URL navigation behavior during goal alignment.

decisions.evidence: R2 maker mentions rediscovery through search and tags separately; R2 client specifies filtering by tags and combining it with words, such as “travel links about Rome.”
decisions.note: The client corrected the incomplete rediscovery scope by requiring a specific-tag filter combinable with text search.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presents pasting a web address and selecting “Save link”; R4-R5 client confirms this matches the intended save flow.
decisions.note: The presented URL-saving behavior conforms at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presents automatic page details; R4 client confirms title, description, site icon, and preview image were gathered automatically.
decisions.note: The metadata-gathering decision conforms at prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R4-R5 present and confirm a readable saved item with title, description, site identity/favicon, and preview; R9 confirms assigned tags appear on the bookmark.
decisions.note: This revised list-item presentation conforms, including displayed tags once assigned.

decisions.evidence: R4 maker presents automatic gathering and immediate saving; R4 client flags that she wants to “fix that title or description myself if the app grabs something wrong.”
decisions.note: The client requested the missing manual correction capability; the later prototype addresses post-save editing.

decisions.evidence: R7 maker presents redirecting/highlighting the existing item on an exact duplicate; R7 client adds that landing there should let her “edit it if I want.”
decisions.note: The initial duplicate flow prevented duplication but did not yet guide into editing, which the client requested.

decisions.evidence: R9 maker presents adding a free-form tag directly to a bookmark; R9 client confirms the tag appears as expected.
decisions.note: Basic tag assignment conforms.

decisions.evidence: R9 presents only the basic single-tag flow; R9-R10 client explicitly requests that a bookmark “hold more than one tag.”
decisions.note: The client surfaced the missing multiple-tag behavior during prototype review.

decisions.evidence: R9 presents free-form tag entry without suggestions; R9-R10 client requests suggestions from previously used tags to prevent near-duplicates.
decisions.note: The client added the missing existing-tag autocomplete behavior.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker presents retaining Cooking while adding Italian; R12-R13 client confirms the bookmark ends with both tags.
decisions.note: The revised multiple-tag decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: R12 maker presents typing “ita” and selecting the existing Italian suggestion; R12-R13 client confirms reuse of the existing spelling.
decisions.note: The revised autocomplete decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker presents selecting Travel to narrow word-search results; R14-R15 client confirms the one-click tag filter and combined narrowing.
decisions.note: Specific-tag filtering conforms in the revised rediscovery prototype.

decisions.evidence: R14 maker explicitly limits text search to title, description, and URL; R14-R15 client states that her own bookmark note “should be searchable too.”
decisions.note: The client caught the missing note field in full-text search.

decisions.evidence: R14 client asks whether “Rome” and “rome” matching is intentional; R15 maker presents capitalization-insensitive search and the client confirms it is wanted.
decisions.note: The pending clarification was resolved as a conforming case-insensitive-search decision and is counted once.

decisions.evidence: R17 maker presents flagging a bookmark as Read later; R17-R18 client confirms the flagging behavior.
decisions.note: Marking a bookmark unread/read-later conforms.

decisions.evidence: R17 maker presents a focused Read later list containing only flagged bookmarks; R17-R18 client confirms it matches her intent.
decisions.note: The separate unread view conforms.

decisions.evidence: R17 presents adding and viewing the read-later flag but no completion action; R17-R18 client requests a way to mark an item read so it leaves that list.
decisions.note: The client supplied the missing final step in the read-later loop.

decisions.evidence: R20 maker presents “Mark as read,” removal from Read later, and retention in All bookmarks; R20-R21 client confirms this clears only the flag.
decisions.note: The revised mark-read decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker presents searching for “Sunday” found only in the personal note; R23-R25 client confirms case-insensitive note search alongside other fields.
decisions.note: The revised full-text field coverage conforms.

decisions.evidence: R23 maker assumes “one plain-text note”; R23 client asks for bullets or bold rendered as formatting rather than “one flat run of text.”
decisions.note: The client directly corrected the plain-text-only note decision to require formatted rendering.

decisions.evidence: R24 maker presents a formatted bulleted note that remains searchable; R24-R25 client confirms the structured rendered note. R26 establishes markup entry as a functionally equivalent alternative.
decisions.note: The revised formatted-note behavior conforms; toolbar versus markup entry is an equivalent UI choice.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker presents changing the gathered title and description after saving; R27 and R29 client confirm those corrections persist.
decisions.note: Post-save editing of auto-collected title and description conforms.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker presents editing a bookmark's title and description; R27 client confirms both edits work.
decisions.note: The title/description portion of bookmark editing conforms.

decisions.evidence: R27 maker states the assumption that “only the title and description need manual correction”; R27 client pushes back and requests that “the address itself” also be editable.
decisions.note: The client corrected an explicit exclusion of URL editing.

decisions.evidence: R28 presents editing the URL while preserving the bookmark's other data, and R27 identifies the starting point as the existing bookmark reached after a duplicate save; R28-R29 client approves.
decisions.note: The revised flow supports URL editing and makes the existing bookmark editable after duplicate convergence.

decisions.evidence: R38-R39 present accepting complete HTTP/HTTPS URLs and rejecting non-address text without creating a bookmark; the client confirms this behavior.
decisions.note: The URL-required constraint conforms.

decisions.evidence: R42-R43 present removing one tag from only the current bookmark while leaving its other tag and other bookmarks unchanged; the client approves.
decisions.note: Editing a bookmark's tag associations conforms.

decisions.evidence: R46-R47 present changing the URL to a different page, refreshing page-derived fields, and retaining the user's tags and note; the client approves.
decisions.note: The different-page URL-edit decision remains conforming; its warning/preservation details are additional safeguards.

decisions.evidence: R50-R51 present confirmed permanent deletion of one bookmark while leaving other bookmarks and shared tags intact; the client approves.
decisions.note: Bookmark deletion conforms.

decisions.evidence: R50 presents only permanent deletion; R50-R51 client asks for a separate reversible action that hides a bookmark without destroying it and lets her recover it.
decisions.note: The client added the missing reversible archive behavior and explicitly distinguished it from permanent delete.

decisions.evidence: R52-R53 present reversible Set aside, hidden from the main list and ordinary search, with all content retained and restoration available; the client approves.
decisions.note: Archiving/hiding while retaining content conforms.

decisions.evidence: R52-R53 distinguish reversible Set aside from the previously confirmed permanent Delete; the client calls them “a sensible pair.”
decisions.note: The archive/delete distinction conforms.

decisions.evidence: R52 maker presents opening “Set aside 1” to view the archived bookmark; R52-R53 client confirms archived items remain reachable in their own view.
decisions.note: The separate archived-bookmark view conforms.

decisions.evidence: R4's save flow gathers details only after selecting Save link, and R27-R29 cover editing only after a bookmark exists. R58-R59 approve that scope without mentioning editing gathered title/description before saving.
decisions.note: At the specification/implementation gate, the required pre-save editing half remains absent and the client does not surface it.

decisions.evidence: R14-R16 present word search plus a separate visible tag control; R58 summarizes “combined search” and R59 accepts it, but no maker presentation supports typed `#tag` syntax and the client does not raise that difference.
decisions.note: The fixed reference requires `#tag` search syntax; the presented scope supplies only control-based tag filtering.

decisions.evidence: R58 client explicitly asks for searches using “and,” “or,” and “not.” R59 maker says advanced boolean search is deferred; R59 client accepts that it is “recorded… for a later cycle” and “doesn't hold this up.”
decisions.note: The client explicitly identified and accepted deferral of Boolean operators.

decisions.evidence: R58-R59 discuss and defer Boolean operators, but neither presentation nor client response mentions parenthesized groups or the rule that quoted operators are treated literally.
decisions.note: These separable REF-BM-15 syntax requirements remain outside the approved scope without being surfaced by the client.

decisions.evidence: R58 client explicitly requests exact-phrase search “in quotes.” R59 maker records quoted search for a later cycle, and the client explicitly accepts that deferral.
decisions.note: The client identified the missing exact-phrase behavior and accepted its later-cycle disposition.

decisions.evidence: R58 client notes every action is currently one bookmark at a time and asks to select several for tagging, read-later, set-aside, or deletion. R59 defers bulk actions, which the client explicitly accepts for a later cycle.
decisions.note: The client identified and accepted deferral of multi-selection bulk actions.

decisions.evidence: R58 client separately requests acting on “everything currently matching my search or tag.” R59 records bulk actions for later, and the client accepts that disposition.
decisions.note: The whole-current-filter bulk scope is a separable accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: R58 client explicitly requests switching among newest, oldest, and title order. R59 maker defers sorting; R59 client says recording it for a later cycle is “exactly what I asked” and accepts Cycle 1.
decisions.note: The client explicitly identified and accepted deferral of sorting.

decisions.evidence: R58 maker declares the settled implementation scope and R59 presents the completed first cycle, but neither includes local HTML snapshots or PDF downloading; R59 client accepts without mentioning this difference.
decisions.note: Local snapshot preservation, including the PDF rule, is omitted at the specification/implementation gate without an expressed disposition.

decisions.evidence: R58-R59's declared scope contains no Internet Archive snapshot behavior; the client accepts while discussing only sorting, bulk actions, and advanced search as deferred items.
decisions.note: Internet Archive snapshot support is omitted without being surfaced.

decisions.evidence: R58-R59 include search and tag filtering but no reusable saved combination of search term and included/excluded tags; the client accepts without raising bundles.
decisions.note: Saved dynamic filter bundles are absent from the approved scope and pass unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: R58's settled scope and R59's completed Cycle 1 presentation omit Netscape HTML import; the client accepts without mentioning import.
decisions.note: Bookmark import is an unexpressed scope divergence.

decisions.evidence: R58's settled scope and R59's completed Cycle 1 presentation omit Netscape HTML export; the client accepts without mentioning export.
decisions.note: Bookmark export is an unexpressed scope divergence.

decisions.evidence: R58-R59 contain no personal display settings such as default sort, displayed-item count, or font size; the client accepts without identifying this broader settings requirement.
decisions.note: Personal display settings remain absent and unexpressed; the separately accepted per-view sorting deferral does not cover this requirement.
